profile.reading: This is Telias Helsinki Data Center, referred to in this registry and industry directories by the shorthand Telia HDC, at Valimotie 5 in the Pitajanmaki district of Helsinki, Finland, opened in 2018. The site is built out to 24 megawatts of IT capacity within a larger 100 megawatt total power allocation, using a closed loop water based cooling system with chilled water supplied around 20 degrees Celsius and returned around 32 degrees, achieving a reported water usage effectiveness below 0.1 liters per kilowatt hour, with direct to chip liquid cooling options supporting GPU racks up to 100 kilowatts each. Telia recovers waste heat from the facility for district heating, reporting roughly 5.65 megawatts of heat delivered to Helsinkis district network as of May 2024. The facility holds Tier III and EN 50600 design certification, LEED Data Center v4.0 certification, CEEDA Design Operate Gold certification, seven separate ISO certifications, PCI DSS compliance, and ISO 27001 information security certification. Telia Finland is the Finnish operating unit of Telia Company, headquartered in Solna, Sweden, and descends from Sonera, Finlands former state telecom operator, which merged with Swedens Telia in 2002 to form TeliaSonera, later renamed simply Telia Company in 2016. Telia Company overall operates across the Nordic and Baltic region, providing mobile, fixed, and enterprise connectivity and infrastructure services in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia, and markets this Helsinki facility specifically toward enterprise and hyperscale customers needing high density, liquid cooled capacity for AI and GPU workloads in the Nordic market, positioning the sites district heating integration and sub 0.1 liter per kilowatt hour water usage as sustainability differentiators relative to conventional air cooled data halls.
